message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.  While exact figures are debated, most historians agree on the following rough totals:

| Side | Approximate casualties (killed, wounded, missing) |
|------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **Allied (British, Dutch‑German, Prussian)** | **≈ 25 000** |
| **French** | **≈ 25 000** |

**Breakdown (approximate)**  

| Category | Allied | French |
|----------|--------|--------|
| Killed | 4 000–5 000 | 4 000–5 000 |
| Wounded | 12 000–15 000 | 12 000–15 000 |
| Missing/Prisoners | 3 000–4 000 | 3 000–4 000 |

These numbers come from contemporary reports and later scholarly estimates.  Variations arise because battlefield records were incomplete, and some wounded were later counted as missing or vice‑versa.  Nonetheless, the consensus is that roughly **50 000 soldiers** (both sides combined) suffered casualties in the single day of fighting at Waterloo.
